key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer improves solar-cell efficiency while using graphene to protect the junction against environmental degradation.
engineering_relevance: The architecture combines optical, electrical, and protective functions to improve planar hybrid photovoltaics without substrate texturing.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer devices against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS for antireflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and moisture barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 ambient days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports only 75 days of ambient aging; longer-term durability and manufacturing-scale graphene barrier integrity remain unestablished.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
